cim: Artificial intelligence impacts on managed security service providers
cim_eredeti: Artificial intelligence impacts on managed security service providers
szoveg_eredeti:
Artificial intelligence is fundamentally reshaping the operational landscape for managed security service providers as firms navigate new governance and automation requirements, as first reported by Channel Insider.

Optiv executives Kathryn Hall, senior vice president of managed security services, and Steve Fielder, vice president of engineering and AI solutions, recently discussed how the firm is integrating advanced technology into its security framework. The strategy focuses on rigorous evaluation of AI security tools and the implementation of robust governance models. By leveraging automation, the company aims to augment the capabilities of security analysts while ensuring human oversight remains central to critical decision-making processes.

The discussion highlights the necessity of continuous exposure management and the importance of incorporating business context into security operations. Furthermore, the transition toward AI-driven security requires organizations to redesign existing workflows and invest in reskilling their internal teams. For IT channel partners, these shifts present opportunities to foster deeper customer relationships. Providers are increasingly tasked with helping clients determine which security functions should remain internal and which require external expertise. As the threat landscape evolves, these adaptations are essential for maintaining effective defense postures and delivering value in an increasingly automated environment.
